svg.aria-label: How to write ۷ ۸ ۹: 3 letters, ۷, ۸, ۹, one after another
svg.title: Writing ۷ ۸ ۹
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ۷, ۸, ۹ (perso-arabic). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ۷: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 487 aligned samples of ۷ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 487 (100%); starts at the top left in 360 (74%) <https://github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db/tree/018b039c0f80d84da16fc9c0f7f629c746a5b3c8/Writepads/NumberGroup>; ۸: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 479 aligned samples of ۸ from 29 native writers; one stroke in 479 (100%); starts at the bottom left in 373 (78%) <https://github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db/tree/018b039c0f80d84da16fc9c0f7f629c746a5b3c8/Writepads/NumberGroup>; ۹: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 452 aligned samples of ۹ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 452 (100%); starts in the right half in 379 (84%) <https://github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db/tree/018b039c0f80d84da16fc9c0f7f629c746a5b3c8/Writepads/NumberGroup>. Source notes on variation: ۷: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 487 samples of ۷, 487 (100%) are one stroke. 360 (74%) start at the top left (and 91, 19%, at the middle left); the lowest point comes in the middle of the stroke in 482 (99%), and 451 (93%) end at the top right: down to the point, then up. POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer. ۸: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 479 samples of ۸, 479 (100%) are one stroke. 373 (78%) start at the bottom left and 324 (68%) first move up; the highest point comes in the middle of the stroke in 463 (97%), and 453 (95%) end at the bottom right: up to the peak, then down. POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer. ۹: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 452 samples of ۹, 452 (100%) are one stroke. 379 (84%) start in the right half, most often at the middle right (151, 33%), and 334 (74%) first move left. 449 (99%) reach the top left after leaving the start, so the loop comes first, and 439 (97%) end at the bottom right: the stem comes last, downward. The loop turns clockwise in 277 (61%). POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer.

Letter 2: stroke order after POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup;
AGPL-3.0, facts only): 479 aligned samples of ۸ from 29 native writers; one stroke in 479 (100%); starts at the bottom left in 373 (78%)
Letter 3: stroke order after POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup;
AGPL-3.0, facts only): 452 aligned samples of ۹ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 452 (100%); starts in the right half in 379 (84%)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
